scope: Fixed-position PSF photometry method comparison on the three retained QR3 D1 cutouts

inputs.science_unit: microjansky per native detector pixel; released SOLIDANGLE converts MJy/sr IMAGE and VARIANCE planes
inputs.flags: existing QR3 D1 conservative bad-pixel policy; invalid pixels excluded from all compared fits

question: Does fitting the known components together with a shared sloped local background reduce incremental-flux error for crowded sources relative to independent fixed-position fits, under a QR3 real-image background and an ePSF template withheld from the fitted exposure?

frozen_design.spatial_holdout: Four equal detector-coordinate quadrants are reported separately; all are evaluation regions and no method or threshold is tuned on their outcomes.
frozen_design.truth: known additive component flux; unknown pre-existing scene flux is eliminated by paired on/off amplitude differences, not treated as zero or independently known
frozen_design.injection_profile: for each science exposure use the nearest ePSF from the next exposure in the pinned three-exposure cycle, transformed through its own WCS at the same sky coordinate; normalize the finite released ePSF to unit sum; record injection and fit zone identifiers
frozen_design.randomness: Seeded site choice and independent archive-variance Gaussian perturbations; random draw seeds and every fit status retained
frozen_design.crowding: real image pixels are retained beneath both injected components; only injection truth is controlled

frozen_methods.description: Current SIEVE fit_flux called independently at each known component position; released same-exposure ePSF and a local constant sky.
Proposed grouped weighted linear fit of all known component amplitudes plus one shared local planar background, on identical valid pixels and fixed positions.

Photutils PSFPhotometry with the same group positions, same fitted-exposure ImagePSF, fixed x/y, same fit window, and local background removed using the shared fit's nuisance-plane solution; used as an implementation baseline, not independent truth.

primary_endpoint.population: paired injection groups with separations 1.0, 1.5, or 2.5 pixels and all components returning finite estimates in both methods
primary_endpoint.metric: median absolute component fractional incremental-flux error; group-level paired bootstrap over injection sites, 10000 resamples, seeded from protocol seed
primary_endpoint.comparison: joint versus independent SIEVE fit; report absolute effect, ratio, 95 percent group-bootstrap interval, denominator and all failures
primary_endpoint.interpretation_gate: call an improvement only if the upper 95 percent interval of the joint-to-independent error ratio is below 1 and the point ratio is at most 0.8; otherwise report no demonstrated improvement or insufficient precision

secondary_metrics: per-method signed and absolute incremental-flux bias and scatter by separation, flux ratio, SNR and spatial quadrant

formal uncertainty calibration under independent archive-variance Gaussian perturbations, using the variance of the paired difference and propagated formal covariance; this is conditional on diagonal variance and does not validate unknown detector covariance
position is fixed by design; no astrometric accuracy or detection completeness claim
false detections and identity correctness are not estimable because no independent source-label catalog is provided
median, p95 and maximum wall time, CPU time, peak RSS, logical I/O and pixels fitted for each method and budget
limits: This is a three-cutout QR3 D1 pilot, not an independent sky cohort or production survey validation.
The cross-exposure injection ePSF is independent of the fitted exposure's selected template but is still from the same release and instrument pipeline.
Real-image differencing isolates additive injected response; it does not validate the unknown baseline scene's total source flux.
Archive variance is diagonal; source Poisson noise and pixel covariance are not added or modeled.
Photutils shares the fitted-exposure ePSF and input pixels, so it is a strong implementation reference, not independent astrophysical truth.
No unconfirmed source identity, discovery, FDR, or sky sensitivity claim is allowed.
